title: Theo and the Compass
premise: Desert ranger Casper Vasquez has chased the thief known only as Theo for a year — the man who stole his family's compass and his name along with it. When a flash flood uncovers a chest bearing the seal of Vessia, a drowned nation erased from maps, both men learn the compass is a salvage key pointing to the Vessian wreck, and that Casper's inheritance is a lie his father built to hide a betrayal. Racing the salvage fleet and the dying dry season, Casper and an uneasy Theo reach the wreck by the sixth tide, where the truth of who betrayed whom forces Casper to choose between the loyalty his father demanded and the identity the wreck restores. He claims the wreck for the river's forgotten people, burns the compass, and lets Theo go — no longer a ranger's son, but his own man.
about_author: Mara Underhill is the pen name of a former river surveyor who spent six seasons charting dry-season waterlines across the basin country. Her fiction is known for landscapes that behave like characters and heroes who keep moving because stopping costs more.

chapters.title: The Man Who Stopped Moving
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A year into tracking Theo across the salt flats, Casper nearly catches him at a waystation and fails again, revealing through flashback that the stolen compass belonged to Casper's dead father. The emotional beat is obsession wearing thin — Casper realizes he chases Theo not for justice but because the chase is the only shape his life has left.

chapters.title: What the River Gives Up
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A flash flood strands Casper at a drowned chapel, where the receding water exposes a chest stamped with Vessia's seal — a nation Casper's father helped erase. Inside: salvage charts and a hollow shaped exactly like his compass. The beat is vertigo; the theft he's been avenging was a key, and his father was part of the erasure.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A dying Vessian salvager tells him the wreck of the Amaranth surfaces only at the season's last six tides, and that the fleet under Captain Ilsa Rehn will strip it for the empire. Casper must reach it first — and only the stolen compass can navigate the shifting channels. Beat: reluctant commitment; the chase becomes a race.

chapters.title: The Thief's Version
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, first time. Theo, camped ahead, is ambushed by Rehn's scouts who want the compass; he escapes and reveals his motive — his grandmother was Vessian, and the compass was hers before Casper's father took it. Beat: moral inversion; the thief has a truer claim than the ranger, and both are chasing their fathers' lies.

chapters.title: Partners of Necessity
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Casper catches Theo at the river fork and, instead of arresting him, proposes an alliance against the fleet. A brutal negotiation scene — knives half-drawn, truths traded as collateral. Beat: wary trust; loyalty to a dead father's version of events begins to crack against Theo's living testimony.

chapters.title: The Drowned Archive
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The pair dives a submerged Vessian archive to learn the wreck's location and finds records proving Casper's father led the raid that drowned Vessia's fleet — and stole the compass from Theo's grandmother. Beat: grief and fury; Casper's identity as a ranger's honest son collapses, and Theo watches his enemy grieve.

chapters.title: Rehn's Bargain
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Captain Rehn corners them at a trading post and offers Casper legitimacy — a commission, his father's name restored — if he hands over Theo and the compass. Beat: the loyalty-vs-truth choice made flesh; Casper stalls, lies to Rehn, and realizes he's become his father, trading people for inheritance.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The race down the dying river: the fleet behind, the channels failing, Theo wounded covering Casper's escape. Casper navigates by memory of his father's charts — using the liar's knowledge to defeat the liar's employers. Beat: loyalty reborn on new terms; they stop being allies of necessity.

chapters.title: The Amaranth
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At the fifth tide they reach the wreck and find Rehn already diving it. In the hold: the Vessian crown records that would restore a nation — and a letter in his father's hand confessing everything, meant for Casper all along. Beat: climax; Casper turns the compass on the fleet's own salvage charges, flooding their operation.

chapters.title: A New Bearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sixth tide. Rehn defeated, Casper gives the records to the river settlements' Vessian descendants, burns the compass, and lets Theo walk away with his grandmother's name cleared. Casper stays — not as a ranger's son chasing a thief, but as the river's keeper. Beat: resolution; inheritance refused, identity chosen, truth kept over loyalty.
